headline: Israel election too close to call as exit polls give Netanyahu bloc slightly fewer seats

members.title: Israel election too close to call as exit polls give Netanyahu bloc slightly fewer seats
members.lead: Early indications suggest it will be some time before the shape of new government and who will lead it is clear Israel election – live updates Rise of Palestinian parties in Knesset will redraw Israel’s political landscape Israel’s election appeared to have delivered no clear winner on Tuesday night after a historic turnout by voters for an election described by some as the most consequential in the country’s history, and marked by a record participation by Israeli Arab voters. Exit polls published on Tuesday evening suggested that the opposition bloc of parties led by the former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, Gadi Eisenkot, would win most seats in the Knesset by a slight margin, edging out Benjamin Netanyahu’s right and far-right coalition despite the prime minister’s Likud emerging as the largest party. members.title: Rise of Palestinian parties in Knesset will redraw Israel’s political landscape
members.lead: Exit polls indicate opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot will have to work with Arab-Israeli leaders to have a hope of governing Israeli elections: live updates The big gains made by Palestinian parties in Israel’s general election pose an urgent and fundamental challenge to the country’s mainstream opposition: either cooperate with Arab Israelis or hand Benjamin Netanyahu a roadmap to political survival. In the wake of Tuesday’s exit polls, the leader of the opposition bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, declared them a victory for “Israel’s Zionist national majority” but the real outcome looks as if it will be far more complex than that.
